display_name: Correct, fire, withdraw, retire or reopen an accepted authorization
description: Accepted-authorization obligations (wgr_d854aa6c). Applies one versioned lifecycle change to an entry recorded with record_accepted_authorization. Every call names entry_id, expected_version (the version the caller read), operation, reason and actor. The compare-and-set on id + version + prior state and the immutable before/after event commit together in one transaction, so a stale writer, a lost race or a failed event append writes nothing, and a replay of a change that already landed is refused stale_version instead of duplicating its event; concurrent terminal changes have exactly one winner. correct: change an accepted entry's act, predicate or authorizing message — any change to the act or predicate names authorizing_message_id, the message that reissued it, and the old predicate stays in the history as withdrawn — and any entry's requesting_peer, owed_by_role or branch_or_request_ref; notes are set or corrected with notes and cleared with clear_notes. Required fields are never cleared: withdraw the entry instead. fire: accepted -> fired, naming the CURRENT predicate verbatim plus the action evidence; it only records the supplied evidence and performs no act, and a withdrawn or superseded predicate never fires. Fired is terminal: it is never reopened and its act and predicate are never rewritten; a distinct new act needs a new record. withdraw / retire: accepted -> withdrawn / retired with a reason and optional evidence. reopen: withdrawn or retired -> accepted only with a fresh authorizing_message_id (never the withdrawn one) and predicate, optionally a new act. Bookkeeping only and open to any caller like the refusal-queue verbs (actor is reported provenance); never landing permission.
embedding_description: Updating an accepted authorization obligation over its life: correcting a reissued predicate, recording that the act fired against the current predicate with evidence, withdrawing or retiring it, or reopening it on a fresh authorization. Versioned so a stale or duplicate write is refused and history keeps every old predicate.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: {"entry_id": "aau_...", "operation": "correct|fire|withdraw|retire|reopen", "status": "changed", "state": "accepted|fired|withdrawn|retired", "version": N, "event_id": "aae_...", "entry": {projection snapshot}} — version is what the next change must name.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Name the entry, the operation and the resulting state. A fire is a record of what the caller already did, not a confirmation that anything ran; after a correction, say which predicate is now current.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One typed state transaction: read accepted_authorization by id, check expected_version and the lifecycle rule, compare-and-set on id + version + prior state, then append one accepted_authorization_event.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: an empty required field (entry_id, operation, reason, actor; fire also needs predicate and evidence; reopen needs authorizing_message_id and predicate). invalid_argument: an unknown operation, an argument the operation does not take, a blank optional field, notes together with clear_notes, or an expected_version that is not an integer >= 1. entry_not_found: no accepted entry has that id. stale_version: expected_version is not the entry's current version, or the entry changed between read and write; nothing was written. invalid_transition: the operation is not legal from the entry's state (fire, withdraw and retire need accepted; reopen needs withdrawn or retired; fired is terminal; a non-accepted entry's act, predicate and authorizing message are history). predicate_mismatch: fire did not name the current predicate verbatim. authorizing_message_required: an act or predicate correction did not name its authorizing message. authorization_not_fresh: reopen reused the withdrawn or retired authorizing message. no_change: the correction changes nothing. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Fix argument errors and resend. stale_version means read the entry again (get_authorization_history or list_held_authorizations), decide on its current version and only then resend; after a fault of unknown outcome a stale_version can mean your own change already landed, so read back before acting. invalid_transition, predicate_mismatch and authorization_not_fresh are lifecycle refusals: do not retry as-is. This verb is never retried automatically.
